title: Lark Ventures prospect brief & outbound drafts
content:
Quick context:
- Lark Ventures: mid-market retail payments + checkout platform. HQ SF, engineering org ~40, ML/data team ~6. Recently raised Series B (rumor: Nov 2024).
- Why this matters: target use-case map well to Redwood: embeddings for search/recommendations, chat-assist for merchant ops, and inference cost/latency are sensitive during checkout flows.

Primary contacts (from LinkedIn + ZoomInfo):
- Morgan Hale — CTO (systems + infra), usually pragmatic, cares about latency/SLOs and total cost.
- Sanjay Rao — Head of ML (applied models), cares about model fidelity and eval reproducibility.
- Jenna Park — Head of Platform / Security (SSO, SOC2 concerns).

Top business triggers / signals:
- They complained on a public forum about current vendor = high variability in latency during traffic spikes.
- Job postings for SRE/infra roles mentioning "latency budgets for checkout".
- Merchant churn cited performance regressions in recommendations.

Initial hypothesis of fit:
- Short term: Replace inference tier for recommendation ranking with Redwood Dedicated -> predictable throughput + lower p99.
- Medium term: Migrate customer-facing chat features to Redwood hosted API with caching + prefix caching to reduce token bill.
- Compliance: They will ask about VPC/private control plane for PII in merchant metadata -> Redwood Private fits.

Notes for discovery call (open questions):
- What is your current p95/p99 token latency for recommendation and for chat? Recent SLA breaches?
- Query distribution: median seq length? Recommendation: batching safe?
- Volume: QPS at peak and tail (holiday spikes)?
- How are you measuring cost today (per-request, monthly GPU hours)?
- Any data residency / encryption at rest requirements? KMS/HSM?
- Who signs the contract — procurement/legal timeline?

Outbound email (short A/B drafts) — keep human, engineer-to-engineer:
Draft A (concise):
Subject: Cut tail latency and token spend for Lark’s checkout recommender
Hey Morgan —
We helped a payments platform reduce 99th‑percentile latency on product recommendations by ~2.3x and cut inference cost 30% using a combination of Dedicated capacity + KV prefix caching. If you have 20 minutes, I can run a quick baseline idea for where we’d expect wins on your workload.
—Avery

Draft B (data-forward):
Subject: Quick idea: stable p99 for recommendation ranking during spikes
Morgan —
Saw your post about tail latency during holiday spikes. With Redwood Dedicated + batching policies we typically hit p99 targets consistently while lowering unit cost; we also provide rollout controls (canary/A‑B) so you don’t risk quality. Want to set up a 30m design call — I’ll bring a short checklist to map out a POC.

Cold call / meeting opener (30–60s):
- Intro: "I’m Avery from Redwood Inference — we build inference stacks so teams hit latency SLOs and predictable unit economics. Quick question: how often do you see your recommender or checkout chat spike beyond your SLA?"
- If they say spikes are rare: "Nice. If you’re open, we can run a lightweight cost/latency audit (no infra changes) and show if there’s easy win via batching/caching."

Common objections + responses (engineer + procurement flavors):
- "We own our models / happy with current infra":
  Rebuttal: "Totally — Redwood is model-agnostic. We deploy your variants; policies let you pin versions and we can act as the reliable inference layer without replacing model code.
  Example proof: we onboarded a proprietary BERT-ranker in 2 sprints with canary rollout and zero model code changes."

- "We can’t move data to a hosted service / compliance concerns":
  Rebuttal: "Understood. We offer Private (VPC + on‑prem package) and KMS/HSM integrations; for POC we can run in your VPC or with a short-lived dedicated infra sandbox.
  Ask: what compliance certs matter most (SOC2, PCI scope)?"

- "Pricing: switching vendors is expensive and unpredictable":
  Rebuttal: "We usually start with a scoped POC cost model (fixed commit or short-term Dedicated trial) and provide token-level cost dashboards so you can see unit economics before committing. Also Optimize analyzes batching/quantization levers so you can forecast savings."

Technical POC plan (3-week lightweight):
- Week 0: alignment call, collect traffic snapshot and model artifacts (weights + sequence distribution).
- Week 1: spin up test endpoint (hosted or dedicated ephemeral), run baseline with 1–2 representative prompts and capture latency/cost.
- Week 2: enable batching + prefix caching + quantized model variant, run A/B against baseline for p95/p99 and cost-per-1000 tokens.
- Week 3: results review and recommended rollout path (canary config + fallback).
Deliverable: short report with latency curves, token cost breakdown, suggested Dedicated sizing.

Measurement / success criteria (internal + for prospect):
- p99 latency improvement target: 1.5–2.5x depending on current tail
- Cost: at least 20% unit cost reduction via batching/caching/quantization
- Nonfunctional: demonstrable safer rollback path + tracing hooks for post-deploy debugging

Internal risks / red flags to monitor:
- Tight procurement windows — legal may push back on Private deal timelines.
- Heavy model customization that requires runtime kernels we don’t support (ask infra team for kernel compatibility checklist).
- They may be deep in an ecosystem with managed GPU provider tied to vendor; highlight our migration helpers and data-import docs.

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Pull recent p99 benchmarks from case study library (deck: "retail-recommender-benchmarks Q4 2024").
- Ask solutions-eng to pre-author a standard Dedicated trial quote we can hand off immediately if discovery looks promising.
- Slack thread to start when meeting scheduled: #g2m-lark-opp with Diego + Priya + sol-eng lead.

To-dos (short):
- [ ] Send intro email to Morgan + Morgan’s CTO peer (cc: Jenna Park).
- [ ] Attach short POC checklist to calendar invite if meeting booked.
- [ ] Prepare 10–minute demo snippet showing p99 tail drop with caching on sample dataset.

Random scratch thoughts / quick wins to test in discovery call:
- Offer a quick "latency alpha" report: run their exported request traces through our simulator to estimate p99 gains without infra changes. Good as a low-friction diagnostic.
- Suggest starting with embeddings for search (lower risk) before moving to real-time recommender flow.

End note: keep everything lightweight and technical-first; their CTO looks for measurable SLO improvements and ML lead wants replicated evals, so emphasize reproducible benchmark artifacts and visible rollback controls.
